title: Beef Short-Rib Biryani

ingredientGroups.title: Beef Marinade
items: 1.5kg Onion deep fried till golden (approx. 500 g yield)

ingredientGroups.title: Rice
items: 1 Mace blade, or ½ blade ground mace

ingredientGroups.title: Final Assembly
items: Pinch of saffron infused in 75ml warm milk (Saffron is optional, but authentic)

steps: Dry Roast: Roast all spices on low heat for 2-3 minutes, stirring continuously.
Cool: Transfer to a plate and let cool completely.
Grind: Blend to a fine, aromatic powder.
Combine beef rib with garlic ginger paste, spices, tomato, yoghurt, and salt.
Add fried 200g fried onions and coriander stalks.
Mix thoroughly, marinate overnight and set aside for cooking.
Heat ghee and beef fat blend.
Add whole spices and sauté until aromatic.
Add marinated beef along with all the marinade, cook out until fat splits.
Add beef stock, cover and simmer for 2.5/3 hours until the beef is tender.
Finish with methi, lemon juice, mint and coriander.
Wash and soak rice for 20 mins
Boil water with spices, lemon juice and salt
Add the rice and cook for 5 mins until 70% cooked (rice is nutty) remove half drain, then allow the rest for a further 2 minutes to cook to 90% (looks cooked but is firm)
Drain, remove hard spices and set aside for layering.
Skim the Fat: Once the curried beef is cooked, skim off some of the excess fat from the top and reserve it for finishing.

First Layer: In the biryani pot (wide pots work best), spread the curried beef evenly across the base. Add the first layer of rice (cooked to 70%) over the beef. Sprinkle with biryani masala, chopped mint, chopped coriander and a generous pinch of biryani masala

Second Layer: Add the second layer of rice (cooked to 90%) over the top. Using a spoon, drizzle some of the reserved curried beef fat evenly across the rice. Sprinkle with generous pinch of biryani masala
Saffron Milk Infusion: Sprinkle the saffron milk over the rice for colour and aroma.
Final Garnish: Finish with another layer of fresh herbs (mint and coriander) and lemon slices. Drizzle 2 tablespoons of kewra water across the top.

Sealing the Pot: Cover with a damp cloth and lid or seal the rim with a couple layers of tightly wrapped foil to trap steam. Place the pot on moderate heat for 5 minutes, then reduce to low heat and cook for 20 minutes.
Resting: Remove from heat and allow the biryani to rest for 20 minutes before opening. This resting period lets the flavours settle and the rice finish steaming.

To Serve: Carefully remove the lid. Using a spatula, go right to the bottom and gently fluff the biryani, lifting rice and meat together without breaking the grains. Serve hot, ensuring each portion carries both rice and beef.
